about: Lines and claims for the Atlas's historical borders that OpenHistoricalMap does not hold. Drawn from the treaty texts and the voyages, not traced from anyone's map; schematic by design, and drawn on the plate as such (a dashed line, a hatch). Built into site/public/data/atlas-eras.topo.json by tools/build-atlas-eras.py.

properties.basis: Treaty of Tordesillas, 7 June 1494: a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands. Where it falls depends on the league and the island taken as origin; readings run from about 42° 30' W to 49° 45' W. Drawn at 48° 30' W, where the OpenHistoricalMap captaincies of Brazil (1534) take it, so the line and the borders agree; pole to pole within the plate.

The northwest coast Spain claimed after the voyages of Juan Pérez (1774), Bruno de Heceta and Bodega y Quadra (1775) and Arteaga and Bodega y Quadra (1779), whose farthest north was about 61° N at Prince William Sound and the Kenai peninsula. A coastal band from 42° N (the line later fixed at Adams-Onís, 1819) to about 152° W, some 200 km deep: a claim on the coast, not a surveyed border. Clipped to the land at build time.
